The large-library behaviour is captured (`shot-44-edge-loadmore.png`, live: `edge.html?state=loadmore`). As you scroll, more bookmarks load in, with a clear **"Loading more bookmarks…"** spinner while the next group is fetched, and a **"Showing 20 of 1,284"** count so you always know the whole size. Critically, **search, filters, counts and sorting run against your entire collection**, not just the portion on screen — the visible cards are just how much has been drawn so far.

That count line also raises the **sorting** point you mentioned. Right now the only ordering we've settled is **newest-first** (the default you approved for the save flow). Your message implies sorting should exist as something applied across the whole collection — so I want to be sure I understand what you mean, without assuming:

- Did you mean **just that the existing newest-first order should always apply across the entire library** (not re-sorting only the loaded chunk)? — in which case nothing new is needed, and I'll record the whole-collection rule.
- Or did you mean you want to **choose between different sort orders** (e.g. newest, oldest, recently updated, title A–Z)? — that's a small new capability we haven't designed yet.

Which did you have in mind? If it's the second, I'll show you a quick sort control; if the first, I'll record it and we can wrap up the edge cases.
